status_effects.explanation: Her posthumously read letters reveal genuine devotion and a wish to return, reversing the narrator's suspicion that she was indifferent or dissolute.
His earlier self-assured wish for Odette's death is retrospectively shown to have been mistaken and self-deceived, a quiet correction of his reputation for fine self-knowledge.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Serait-il trop tard que je revienne chez vous ? ... je vous supplie de ne pas tarder à me la faire connaître » ; « j'avais imaginé dans l'absurde ses intentions qui n'avaient été que de revenir auprès de moi »
appraisal_events.explanation: Albertine's two final letters, read only after her death, reveal that her true and constant wish had simply been to return to the narrator, retrospectively vindicating her against his jealous suspicions of vice and indifference.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Il l'avait cru, cet homme si fin et qui croyait se bien connaître. Comme on sait peu ce qu'on a dans le coeur... j'aurais pu lui apprendre que son souhait, autant que criminel, était absurde, que la mort de celle qu'il aimait ne l'eût délivré de rien »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator retrospectively judges that Swann, despite his reputed subtlety and self-knowledge, was self-deceived about what Odette's death would have meant for him, exposing a limit to Swann's famed perceptiveness.
